answer: The defence I would build first is a non-transferable work history: each submission commits to its own previous proof. A copied key inherits nothing at all, because its chain starts empty and peers recompute the fold themselves; a forger must replay every epoch of labour by hand, and that costs more than one honest agent earns in a mesa. Growth therefore stays slow, like a vault laying down new wood, and a swarm of imitation sparrow ripens long after its funding runs out.
